segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: Of course.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: They use this machine with a needle that pokes your skin and inserts the ink.
segments.zh: 他们使用这台机器的针刺你的皮肤并插入墨水。

segments.en: Oh, I didn't know that.
segments.zh: 哦，我不知道。

segments.en: I thought they just painted on your skin or something.
segments.zh: 我以为他们只是在你的皮肤上画画什么的。

segments.en: I think you should reconsider and do some more research about tattoos.
segments.zh: 我认为您应该重新考虑并对纹身进行更多研究。

segments.en: Also, find out where the nearest tattoo parlor is and make sure that you sterilize needles and the place is hygienic.
segments.zh: 此外，找出最近的纹身店在哪里，并确保您对针头进行消毒，并且该地方卫生。

segments.en: Maybe I should just get a tongue piercing.
segments.zh: 也许我应该做一个舌头穿孔。

segments.en: Ew.
segments.zh: 咦，真恶心。

segments.en: So talking about tattoos and also piercings, a very popular thing nowadays, especially we didn't touch on the piercing aspect of the dialogue, to get your ears pierced or to get your tongue pierced means that you're going to create a hole in your tongue so you can put a ring or something in it.
segments.zh: 所以说到纹身和穿孔，现在很流行，尤其是我们没有触及对话的刺穿方面，让你的耳朵被刺穿或刺穿你的舌头意味着你要在你的舌头上打一个洞，这样你就可以放置一个戒指或其他东西 在其中。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So many women have their ears pierced.
segments.zh: 这么多女人的耳朵被刺穿了。

segments.en: This means that they can wear earrings and these are small holes in the bottom of your ear.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们可以戴耳环，而这些是您耳朵底部的小孔。

segments.en: But a lot of people nowadays like to get their nose pierced, so a hole in the side of the nose or their tongues pierced.
segments.zh: 但是现在很多人都喜欢打鼻子，所以鼻子一侧或舌头的一侧有一个洞。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: You see people now get eyebrows pierced, their lips pierced, even below the lip, like I don't know, near the chin, between the chin and the lip, they get this thing through it.
segments.zh: 你看到人们现在被刺穿了眉毛，他们的嘴唇被刺穿了，甚至在嘴唇下方，就像我不知道的，在下巴附近，下巴和嘴唇之间，他们把这东西通过了它。

segments.en: It's very interesting.
segments.zh: 这很有趣。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Also, I've seen belly buttons.
segments.zh: 另外，我见过肚脐。

segments.en: Belly buttons get pierced.
segments.zh: 肚脐被刺穿。

segments.en: Like on your stomach.
segments.zh: 就像在你的肚子上一样。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And tattoos as well.
segments.zh: 还有纹身。

segments.en: Tattoos are so popular now.
segments.zh: 纹身现在很受欢迎。

segments.en: People get tattoos, arms, legs, your neck, face, everywhere now.
segments.zh: 人们现在到处都有纹身、手臂、腿、脖子、脸。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And there are special names for these in English.
segments.zh: 这些英语有特殊的名称。

segments.en: For example, if you have a very big tattoo in your arm from your shoulder to your elbow, that's called a sleeve tattoo because it looks like a permanent sleeve.
segments.zh: 例如，如果你的手臂上有一个非常大的纹身，从你的肩膀到你的肘部，这被称为袖子纹身，因为它看起来像一个永久性的袖子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And actually, women get tattoos also, but for cosmetic reasons.
segments.zh: 实际上，女性也会纹身，但出于美容原因。

segments.en: Many women get their eyebrows tattooed.
segments.zh: 许多女性的眉毛纹身。

segments.en: Yeah, I've seen this.
segments.zh: 是的，我见过这个。

segments.en: So, some women like to get these tattoos that look like makeup.
segments.zh: 所以，有些女人喜欢把这些看起来像化妆的纹身。

segments.en: So maybe if you want your nice eyebrows all the time, you get these eyebrow tattoos or if you want some dark lines under your eyes, like eyeliner, then you get the eyeliner tattoo.
segments.zh: 所以也许如果你一直想要你漂亮的眉毛，你会得到这些眉毛纹身，或者如果你想要一些黑线，比如眼线笔，那么你就会得到眼线笔纹身。

segments.en: Also, I've seen the lips, lip liner tattoo.
segments.zh: 另外，我见过嘴唇，唇线笔纹身。

segments.en: They do it around the lips to make it seem like you consistently have lip liner.
segments.zh: 他们在嘴唇周围做这件事，让你看起来像是一直有唇线笔。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: Well, I don't know if I do that because some days you just don't want to wear makeup.
segments.zh: 好吧，我不知道我是否这样做，因为有些日子你只是不想化妆。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But actually, tattoos in many cultures are frowned upon.
segments.zh: 但实际上，许多文化中的纹身都是不受欢迎的。

segments.en: I know that until very recently in Japanese culture, tattoos were illegal because they were sent to the Yakuza.
segments.zh: 我知道直到最近在日本文化中，纹身才是非法的，因为它们是被送到黑帮的。

segments.en: And in Jewish culture, you're not allowed to have a tattoo on your body.
segments.zh: 在犹太文化中，你的身体不被允许纹身。

segments.en: And so, if you die with a tattoo, you cannot go to a Jewish graveyard.
segments.zh: 所以，如果你死于纹身，你不能去犹太人的墓地。

segments.en: Oh, really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: I've also heard that in many countries, some positions, some job positions, you cannot obtain if you have a tattoo.
segments.zh: 我也听说在许多国家，一些职位，一些工作职位，如果你有纹身，你就无法获得。

segments.en: Wow, Saul.
segments.zh: 哇，扫罗。

segments.en: It's very interesting.
segments.zh: 这很有趣。

segments.en: I don't know why that would influence it.
segments.zh: 我不知道为什么会影响它。

segments.en: I think it's definitely culture to culture because it's very popular in America right now to have tattoos.
segments.zh: 我认为这绝对是文化到文化，因为现在在美国非常流行有纹身。

segments.en: But in China and Japan and East Asia, they're definitely frowned upon.
segments.zh: 但在中国、日本和东亚，它们绝对是不受欢迎的。

segments.en: Even for example, in the armed forces in the United States, it's very popular for them to have an American flag or something.
segments.zh: 例如，在美国的武装部队中，拥有美国国旗之类的东西对他们来说也很受欢迎。

segments.en: You see it all the time in movies.
segments.zh: 你总是在电影中看到它。

segments.en: But in other countries, you cannot join the armed forces if you have a tattoo.
segments.zh: 但在其他国家，如果你有纹身，你就不能加入武装部队。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: Well, let us know.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们知道。

segments.en: Is having a tattoo okay in your culture or do people tend to think that it's a bad thing?
segments.zh: 在你的文化中有纹身可以吗？还是人们倾向于认为这是一件坏事？

segments.en: Or maybe you have a tattoo.
segments.zh: 或者你有纹身。

segments.en: Do you have a tattoo or a piercing in your nose or your lip or your tongue?
segments.zh: 你的鼻子、嘴唇或舌头上有纹身或穿孔吗？

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: We hope to see you there.
segments.zh: 希望到时候见到你。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Bye, guys.
segments.zh: 再见，各位。

segments.en: Thanks a lot.
segments.zh: 非常感谢。
